newsitem.title: USA: Eighth arrest made in New York deaf-mute case.
newsitem.headline: Eighth arrest made in New York deaf-mute case.

text.p: A deaf Mexican living with dozens of illegal immigrants rescued from servitude was arrested on Tuesday and accused of being part of the ring that allegedly smuggled deaf-mute Mexicans into the United States.

Ivan Gomez Sanchez, 24, an illegal Mexican immigrant who also is deaf, was arrested at a motel where 62 Mexican immigrants had been staying since they were found in near-slavery conditions on July 18.
Police had mistakenly assumed he was one of the victims, authorities said.
Instead, federal officials described Sanchez as an enforcer in one of the two New York City apartments where the immigrants had allegedly been held captive.

He was arraigned in Brooklyn federal court on charges of conspiracy to smuggle illegal aliens into the United States and hiding them from authorities. If convicted, he faces seven years in prison on each of several conspiracy counts.
Seven other people have been charged in the case. However, investigators say they are still seeking the alleged ringleader, identified as Reinaldo Paoletti.
The existence of the alleged ring was revealed on July 18 when one of the deaf-mute Mexicans and another man walked into a New York City police precinct and explained their plight.
They said they were held in virtual slavery since being recruited in Mexico and had hoped for a better life in the United States.
They said they were forced to work seven days a week selling trinkets on city subways and in city streets.
Authorities said Sanchez gave the aliens the trinkets to sell, took their money at the end of each day and threatened them with violence to keep them in line.

Sanchez was not in either of the two apartments when the alleged ring was exposed and went to police to determine what happened, his attorney said. His attorney said his client was a victim and not part of the alleged ring.
A federal magistrate ordered Sanchez held in jail pending further action. The case is expected to go before a grand jury to determine if an indictment will be brought.
Similar rings have since been discovered in Sanford, North Carolina, and in Chicago.
